rulesTds: Higher of the prescribed rate, rates in force, or 20%. 5% for purchase of goods and e-commerce [s.397(2)(b)(i)]. Rent under Sl. 2(i) is capped at the last month’s rent.
Payments to residents and domestic companies: none on TDS. Non-residents and foreign companies: applicable surcharge plus 4% cess. Salary: as per Part III, with 4% cess [Finance Act 2026, s.3].

Non-resident individual, HUF, AOP or BOI: 10% above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore, 25% above ₹2 crore, 37% above ₹5 crore; at most 25% under the new regime, and at most 15% on dividend and capital gains. AOP of companies only: 10% above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore. Non-resident co-operative: 7% above ₹1 crore, 12% above ₹10 crore. Non-resident firm: 12% above ₹1 crore. Foreign company: 2% above ₹1 crore, 5% above ₹10 crore. Limits are on the amount paid or likely to be paid [Finance Act 2026, s.3(7)].
Where the agreement shows GST on services separately, deduct TDS on the amount excluding GST [CBDT Circular 23/2017, continued by s.536(2)(j)].
Payee located in a notified area: highest of the specified rate, rates in force or 30% [s.176(5)]. No area is notified at present; Cyprus was removed with effect from 1-11-2013.
For payments to non-residents, the treaty rate applies if lower, when the payee gives a tax residency certificate. See the DTAA withholding rates tile.
Payee applies in Form 128 for a s.395 certificate. Quote reason flag A in the return.
At credit or payment, whichever is earlier. Salary, winnings, cash withdrawal, EPF and similar: at payment.
rulesTcs: Higher of twice the rate or 5%, capped at 20% [s.397(2)(b)(ii)]. Not applicable to a non-resident without a permanent establishment in India.
Resident collectee: none. Non-resident collectee: surcharge at the same slabs as TDS on non-residents, plus 4% cess [Finance Act 2026, s.3(9)].
At debit to the buyer’s account or receipt, whichever is earlier.
A resident buyer using goods at Sl. 1–5 for manufacturing, processing or power (not trading) can give Form 127. No TCS then.
Public sector companies, Government, embassies and similar missions, clubs, and retail buyers for personal consumption [s.402(6)].
TCS on sale of goods has no equivalent in section 394.

specified.title: Specified person
specified.text: Any person other than an individual or HUF. An individual or HUF is also a specified person if its business turnover exceeded ₹1 crore, or its professional receipts exceeded ₹50 lakh, in the tax year before the payment.

designated.title: Designated person
designated.text: Central or State Government, local authorities, statutory corporations, companies, co-operative societies, housing and planning authorities, registered societies, trusts, universities, foreign governments and enterprises, and firms. An individual, HUF, AOP or BOI is included if its business turnover exceeded ₹1 crore, or its professional receipts exceeded ₹50 lakh, in the preceding tax year.

inforce.title: Rates in force
inforce.text: Where the Table says rates in force, the rate comes from the Finance Act for the year: Part II of the First Schedule for most payments, and the Part III slab rates for salary and specified senior citizens. Salary TDS is at the average rate on the estimated income for the year.
inforce.ref: Finance Act, 2026, s.3(7) and (10); Income-tax Act, 2025, s.392(1)

nopan.title: Payee without PAN
nopan.text: TDS is at the highest of the rate in the Act, the rates in force, or 20% (5% for purchase of goods and e-commerce). TCS is at twice the rate or 5%, whichever is higher, capped at 20%. Rent under Sl. 2(i) is capped at the last month's rent.

form141.title: Form 141 cases
form141.text: Rent paid by individuals and HUFs who are not specified persons, purchase of immovable property, contract or professional payments by individuals and HUFs, and VDA paid by individuals and HUFs. The deductor pays and reports through Form 141 within 30 days from the end of the month of deduction, quoting PAN instead of TAN. The quarterly formats have no payment code for these.

f141Note: Form 141 cases have no code in the quarterly formats. Blogs report 1007 (rent), 1010 (property), 1025 (individual/HUF contractor) and 1036 (VDA), but these could not be confirmed against an official source. Follow the portal screen.
